name: A10-0282/2026 – Aurore Lalucq – Commission proposal to the Council
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council directive amending Directive 2006/112/EC as regards the extension of the application period of the optional reverse charge mechanism in relation to supplies of certain goods and services susceptible to fraud and of the Quick Reaction Mechanism against VAT fraud
part_text:
The European Parliament approves a plan to keep two anti-VAT-fraud tools available to European Union countries until 30 June 2030. One tool lets a country make the buyer, not the seller, pay the VAT on certain goods and services that are often targeted by fraud. The other lets a country act fast against sudden, large-scale VAT fraud. Both tools currently expire at the end of 2026. The extra time bridges the gap until new digital reporting rules apply from 1 July 2030.

- **What changes:** The two anti-fraud tools stay available until 30 June 2030 instead of expiring on 31 December 2026.
- **Who it affects:** European Union countries and their tax authorities; businesses in sectors prone to VAT fraud.
- **What happens next:** The Council of the European Union decides; Parliament must be told if the Council changes the text.
